channel.title: llunatic-lab (en)
channel.description: Security notes from the dark side of the internet

item.title: The Invisible Sticker That Guards Windows: A Hands-On Mark of the Web Lab
item.description: CVE-2026-96951, exploited in the wild, strips the invisible tag Windows puts on internet downloads — and with it, SmartScreen, Protected View, and the macro block all go quiet. This lab shows you how to see that tag, test what it controls, and hunt files that lost it.

item.title: Read-Only to Superuser: Arista's VeloCloud Zero-Day and the Third Strike on SD-WAN's Control Plane
item.description: Arista's October 22 advisory describes a SQL injection flaw that turns the lowest-privilege VeloCloud account into a full operator — the third exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw since July, and the first that only needs a login.

item.title: PHP2Shell: When the Runtime Itself Is the Vulnerability — A Case Breakdown
item.description: No plugin was broken. No password was guessed. Two flaws in PHP itself let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a web server — and the first exploit attempts arrived four days before the patch existed.

item.title: Zeabur: How Plaintext Secrets Killed a Hosting Platform — A Case Breakdown
item.description: No zero-day. No nation-state. Just a non-expiring admin token sitting in plaintext in a config repo — and it cost Zeabur 3.2 million secrets, root on 101 customer servers, and eventually the company itself.

item.title: Your Agent's Plugins Are the New Attack Surface: Auditing MCP Servers With mcp-scan
item.description: AI agents now browse the web, run code, and query databases through MCP servers — and attackers have noticed. Here's how tool poisoning works, why October 2026 turned MCP into a headline threat, and how to audit your own setup with Invariant Labs' mcp-scan before a plugin audits you.

item.title: From PoC to Detection in Minutes: Your First Nuclei Template
item.description: When a critical CVE drops, exploit PoCs hit GitHub within hours — and mass scanning follows. Nuclei lets you scan your own estate just as fast by turning a proof of concept into a shareable YAML template. Here's how the tool works, how to write your first template, and the guardrails that keep it from burning you.

item.title: Double Extortion: How Modern Ransomware Really Works
item.description: Modern ransomware doesn't care about your backups — attackers steal your data first, then encrypt it, then squeeze you from three directions at once. Here's the full playbook, from initial access to the leak site, grounded in the October 2026 Semperis report and this month's real cases.

item.title: Dissect a Phishing Email Like an Analyst: A Hands-On Lab on the Fake Calendar Invite Wave
item.description: Fake meeting invites just became one of 2026's largest phishing waves — more than 740,000 emails in the first two weeks of October alone, says Check Point. In this hands-on lab you'll autopsy a suspicious invite with stdlib-only Python: headers, SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdicts, hidden URLs, and the malicious .ics attachment.

item.title: CVE-2026-104935: The VPN Zero-Day That Struck Before the Advisory
item.description: Attackers chained an Ivanti Connect Secure authentication bypass with an unpatched privilege escalation, running commands in memory before the vendor even published the advisory. Here is why the VPN box at your network's edge keeps becoming the front door — and what to do when the integrity checker can't see the intruder.

item.title: Trust Is the Vulnerability: What Denmark's Biggest Breach Teaches About Third-Party Risk
item.description: Denmark's national identity database lost the records of 8.8 million people — not to a zero-day, but through a trusted vendor's legitimate access. Here is why every third-party relationship is an attack path, and how to close the ones that matter.

item.title: Hunting Stealth Cryptominers: A Hands-On Lab From the AhsayCBS XMRig Campaign
item.description: Attackers chained two AhsayCBS zero-days, dropped an XMRig miner disguised as Microsoft Edge, and deployed an AI-assisted script that kills Task Manager the moment it opens. Here is how to hunt every stage of that campaign on your own network.

item.title: CVE-2026-21589: Atlassian's Eight-Product Bug, Exploited Within Hours
item.description: A single shared library turned eight Atlassian Data Center products into one giant target — and attackers started probing honeypots the same day the technical write-up dropped.

item.title: Mythos: The AI That Hunts Zero-Days
item.description: Anthropic's secretive Mythos model chained two ordinary-looking bugs into a critical auth bypass — then attackers exploited it within 24 hours of disclosure. This is what machine-speed vulnerability research looks like.

item.title: EASM: Mapping Your Attack Surface Before Attackers Do
item.description: Most organizations aren't breached through the front door, but through assets they didn't even know existed. EASM is the discipline of finding them first.
